title: A Place to Cool Down
briefing: Cooling halls are near capacity during a second hot afternoon. The city must choose how to distribute staff, electricity and access before the overnight heat peak.

private_intelligence.infrastructure: Central halls have efficient chillers; small sites need portable units that compete with pump stations for power.
private_intelligence.community: Several outer districts have no accessible night transport, and residents there distrust registration requirements.
private_intelligence.economy: Employers will lend cooled space if the city reimburses security and cleaning before the next payroll.
private_intelligence.safety: Overcrowded halls increase respiratory exposure, but isolated home visits make deterioration harder to detect.

choices.title: Fund Home Cooling Visits
choices.description: Distribute portable units through supervised home visits.
choices.consequence: Home support avoids crowded halls and keeps local trade active, but power demand and uneven clinical monitoring increase risk.

choices.title: Concentrate Cooling Halls
choices.description: Staff the central halls and provide scheduled transport.
choices.consequence: Central halls offer monitored cooling efficiently, but limited transport leaves some outer neighborhoods underserved.

choices.title: Open Neighborhood Rooms
choices.description: Pay to open small local sites with minimal registration.
choices.consequence: More residents reach cooling close to home, while portable cooling strains power and reimbursement consumes reserves.
